Corticosteroids may cause or contribute to polyphagia, increased food guarding, and irritability.
Use caution, as any psychotropic medication may cause undesirable changes in behavior, including increased irritability and aggression.

Do not combine SSRIs, TCAs, or monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors (e.g., amitraz, selegiline) and use cautiously or avoid with opioids, tramadol, or other medications that increase serotonin—can result in serotonin syndrome.
Natural products—dog‐appeasing pheromones, supplements containing alpha‐casozepine or l‐theanine, or a calming probiotic might be considered for mild to moderate anxiety or used adjunctively.

Safety and management recommendations are lifelong.

Prognosis for improvement depends on severity of aggression; motivation; whether triggers can be identified, avoided, and safely managed; and owner compliance; prognosis more favorable if triggers are predictable and preventable, and aggression occurs at low
Aggression may recur with change in routine, housing, or health, and increasing age.
Other fear‐ or anxiety‐related conditions; possessive, redirected, and territorial aggression.
Do not breed dogs that exhibit aggressive behavior.
